questions.question_html:
Question 6 of 60
6. Question

Which two statements are true regarding the UNION and UNION ALL operators? (Choose two.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

The two true statements regarding the UNION and UNION ALL operators are:

The number of columns selected in each SELECT statement must be identical. This is crucial for these operators to function correctly. They combine results vertically, so the columns from each SELECT statement must align properly to form a coherent result set.

NULLs are not ignored during duplicate checking. This means that two NULL values in the same column are considered duplicates by both UNION and UNION ALL. They won‘t be eliminated during the merging process unless specifically instructed to do so using additional filters or conditions.

Here‘s why the other statements are incorrect:

The output is sorted by the UNION ALL operator: This is not true. Neither UNION nor UNION ALL automatically sort the results. You need to explicitly use an ORDER BY clause if you want the output in a specific order.
Duplicates are eliminated automatically by the UNION ALL operator: This is a characteristic of the UNION operator, not UNION ALL. UNION ALL retains all rows, including duplicates, while UNION removes duplicates to produce a distinct set of results.
The names of columns selected in each SELECT statement must be identical: This is not strictly required. While it‘s often recommended for consistency, the columns only need to have compatible data types and positions in the result set. The names can differ, but their order and data types must match.

Correct

CONSTRAINT clause
A CONSTRAINT clause is an optional part of a CREATE TABLE statement or ALTER TABLE statement. A constraint is a rule to which data must conform. Constraint names are optional.
A CONSTRAINT can be one of the following:
a column-level constraint
Column-level constraints refer to a single column in the table and do not specify a column name (except check constraints). They refer to the column that they follow.
a table-level constraint
Table-level constraints refer to one or more columns in the table. Table-level constraints specify the names of the columns to which they apply. Table-level CHECK constraints can refer to 0 or more columns in the table.
Column constraints include:
NOT NULL
Specifies that this column cannot hold NULL values (constraints of this type are not nameable).
PRIMARY KEY
Specifies the column that uniquely identifies a row in the table. The identified columns must be defined as NOT NULL.
Note: If you attempt to add a primary key using ALTER TABLE and any of the columns included in the primary key contain null values, an error will be generated and the primary key will not be added. See ALTER TABLE statement for more information.
UNIQUE
Specifies that values in the column must be unique.
FOREIGN KEY
Specifies that the values in the column must correspond to values in a referenced primary key or unique key column or that they are NULL.
CHECK
Specifies rules for values in the column.
Table constraints include:
PRIMARY KEY
Specifies the column or columns that uniquely identify a row in the table. NULL values are not allowed.
UNIQUE
Specifies that values in the columns must be unique.
FOREIGN KEY
Specifies that the values in the columns must correspond to values in referenced primary key or unique columns or that they are NULL.

Question 16 of 60
16. Question

Which three statements are true about the Oracle Data Dictionary? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

Data Dictionary views are created by joins of dictionary base tables, not DBA-defined tables.
These are owned by SYS, not SYSTEM user.
Contents of the Data Dictionary
The data dictionary consists of base tables and views.
These objects are defined as follows:
Base tables
These store information about the database. Only Oracle Database should write to and read these tables. Users rarely access the base tables directly because they are normalized and most data is stored in a cryptic format.
Views
These decode the base table data into useful information, such as user or table names, using joins and WHERE clauses to simplify the information. The views contain the names and description of all objects in the data dictionary. Some views are accessible to all database users, whereas others are intended for administrators only.
Read here – Contents of the Data Dictionary
How Oracle Database Uses the Data Dictionary
The Oracle Database user account SYS owns all base tables and user-accessible views of the data dictionary.

questions.question_html:
Question 17 of 60
17. Question

You want to apply the principle of Least Privilege in all your live databases.
One of your requirements is to revoke unnecessary privileges from all users who have them using Privilege Analysis.
Which three types of analyses can be done using the DBMS_PRIVILEGE_CAPTURE package? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

Correct:

Option A. analysis of privileges granted indirectly to a role that are then used by a user who has been granted that role
Privilege Analysis using the DBMS_PRIVILEGE_CAPTURE package can track privileges that are not granted directly to a user but are inherited through roles. This includes identifying which role-based privileges are actually exercised by users, which is essential for enforcing Least Privilege and safely revoking unused role privileges.

Option C. analysis of all privileges used by all users but excluding administrative users in the database
DBMS_PRIVILEGE_CAPTURE supports database-level privilege capture that can be scoped to exclude administrative users. This allows organizations to focus on application and business users, making it easier to identify and revoke unnecessary privileges without impacting critical DBA or system accounts.

Option E. analysis of privileges granted directly to a role that are then used by a user who has been granted that role
The package can analyze privileges granted directly to roles and determine whether those privileges are actually used by users who inherit them. This is a core capability of Privilege Analysis and is specifically designed to support Least Privilege by identifying unused role privileges.

Incorrect:

Option B. analysis of privileges that a user has on their own schema objects that they did use
Privilege Analysis focuses on system privileges, object privileges, and role usage. Privileges on a user’s own schema objects are implicitly available and not the primary target of privilege capture analysis, making this option incorrect.

Option D. analysis of all privileges used by all users including administrative users in the database
Including administrative users (such as SYS or users with powerful administrative roles) is not supported for standard Privilege Analysis captures. Oracle explicitly limits or excludes administrative users from such analyses to avoid skewed results and protect system integrity.

Option F. analysis of privileges that a user has on their own schema objects that they did not use
Privileges on a user’s own schema objects are not typically evaluated for usage or non-usage in Privilege Analysis. The feature is intended to analyze granted privileges (system, object, and role-based), not implicit ownership privileges, so this option is incorrect.

This includes identifying which role-based privileges are actually exercised by users, which is essential for enforcing Least Privilege and safely revoking unused role privileges.

Option C. analysis of all privileges used by all users but excluding administrative users in the database
DBMS_PRIVILEGE_CAPTURE supports database-level privilege capture that can be scoped to exclude administrative users. This allows organizations to focus on application and business users, making it easier to identify and revoke unnecessary privileges without impacting critical DBA or system accounts.

Option E. analysis of privileges granted directly to a role that are then used by a user who has been granted that role
The package can analyze privileges granted directly to roles and determine whether those privileges are actually used by users who inherit them. This is a core capability of Privilege Analysis and is specifically designed to support Least Privilege by identifying unused role privileges.

Incorrect:

Option B. analysis of privileges that a user has on their own schema objects that they did use
Privilege Analysis focuses on system privileges, object privileges, and role usage. Privileges on a user’s own schema objects are implicitly available and not the primary target of privilege capture analysis, making this option incorrect.

Option D. analysis of all privileges used by all users including administrative users in the database
Including administrative users (such as SYS or users with powerful administrative roles) is not supported for standard Privilege Analysis captures. Oracle explicitly limits or excludes administrative users from such analyses to avoid skewed results and protect system integrity.

Option F. analysis of privileges that a user has on their own schema objects that they did not use
Privileges on a user’s own schema objects are not typically evaluated for usage or non-usage in Privilege Analysis. The feature is intended to analyze granted privileges (system, object, and role-based), not implicit ownership privileges, so this option is incorrect.

Correct

Option A. A segment can span multiple data files in some tablespaces

  • Correct because in locally managed tablespaces, a segment can extend across multiple data files if the tablespace consists of more than one data file.

Option C. A segment might have only one extent

  • Correct because when a segment is first created, it may consist of just a single extent. Over time, more extents can be allocated as data grows.

questions.question_html:
Question 23 of 60
23. Question

Which two statements are true about space-saving features in an Oracle Database? (Choose two.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

Correct

Option A. Private Temporary Tables (PTTs) store metadata in memory only

  • Correct because PTTs are designed to reduce space usage.
  • Their metadata is stored in memory, not in the data dictionary, which saves space and improves performance.

Option D. An index created with the UNUSABLE attribute has no segment

  • Correct because when an index is created with the UNUSABLE attribute, Oracle does not allocate a segment for it.
  • This is a space-saving feature since the index structure exists logically but consumes no physical storage until rebuilt.

Incorrect

Option B. A table that is truncated will always have its segment removed

  • Incorrect because truncating a table does not always remove its segment.
  • By default, the segment remains allocated, though rows are deleted. Segment removal only occurs if explicitly specified with DROP STORAGE.

Option C. An index that is altered to be UNUSABLE will retain its segment

  • Incorrect because altering an index to UNUSABLE makes it unavailable for use, but its segment is not dropped automatically.
  • This statement is misleading in the context of space-saving features.

Option E. Private Temporary Tables (PTTs) are always dropped at the next COMMIT or ROLLBACK

  • Incorrect because PTTs persist until the end of the session, not just after a commit or rollback.
  • Dropping at commit/rollback applies to global temporary tables, not private temporary tables.

24. Question

Which four account management capabilities can be configured using Oracle profiles? (Choose four.)

  • 1.
  • 2.

Correct

Correct

Option A. The number of days for which an account is locked after the configured number of login attempts has been reached

  • Explanation:
    • Profiles allow you to configure FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS and PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME.
    • This means you can set how long an account remains locked after failed login attempts.

Option C. The number of hours for which an account is locked after the configured number of login attempts has been reached

  • Explanation:
    • Similar to Option A, but expressed in hours.
    • Oracle profiles allow fine-grained control of lock duration using PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME.

Option E. The number of days for which an account may be inactive before it is locked

  • Explanation:
    • This is controlled by PASSWORD_INACTIVE_TIME in profiles.
    • It specifies how long an account can remain inactive before being locked.

  • Explanation:

25. Question

Which two are true about a SQL statement using SET operators such as UNION? (Choose two.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

Correct

  • Option B. The data type group of each column returned by the second query must match the data type of the corresponding column returned by the first query
    • Oracle requires that corresponding columns in each SELECT of a set operator belong to the same data type group (e.g., numeric, character, date).
    • Exact matches are not required, but they must be compatible within the same group.
  • Option C. The number, but not names, of columns must be identical for all SELECT statements in the query
    • All SELECT statements in a set operator must return the same number of columns.

questions.preview: Which three are types of segments in an Oracle Database? (Choose three.)
questions.question_html:
Question 26 of 60
26. Question

Which three are types of segments in an Oracle Database? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

Correct

Option A. Clusters

  • Correct because a cluster segment stores data for tables that are grouped together based on common columns.
  • It is a valid type of segment in Oracle databases.

Option B. Index

  • Correct because an index segment stores the index structures created on tables or clusters.
  • Indexes are separate segments that improve query performance.

Option F. Tables

  • Correct because a table segment stores the actual rows of a table.
  • Each non‑clustered table has its own segment.

Incorrect

Option C. Undo

  • Incorrect because undo is stored in undo tablespaces, but it is managed as undo segments internally.
  • However, in the context of this exam question, the focus is on user‑visible segment types like tables, indexes, and clusters. Undo is not typically listed among the standard segment types for this exam objective.

Option D. Stored Procedures

  • Incorrect because stored procedures are PL/SQL objects, not segments.
  • They are stored in the data dictionary, not as separate segments.

Option E. Sequences

  • Incorrect because sequences are database objects used to generate numeric values, but they do not have associated segments.
  • They are metadata objects, not storage segments.

Question 27 of 60
27. Question

Which two statements are true about the DUAL table? (Choose two.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

Correct

Option C. It consists of a single row and single column of VARCHAR2 data type

  • Correct because the DUAL table is a special one‑row, one‑column table automatically created by Oracle.
  • It is primarily used for evaluating expressions, constants, and pseudo columns without needing to reference actual user tables.

Option E. It can be accessed by any user who has the SELECT privilege in any schema

  • Correct because the DUAL table is available to all users.
  • Any user with basic SELECT privileges can query DUAL, making it universally accessible across schemas.

Incorrect

Option A. It can be accessed only by the SYS user

questions.question_html:
Question 29 of 60
29. Question

In which three situations does a new transaction always start? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

Correct

Option B. CREATE INDEX after CREATE TABLE

  • Correct because DDL statements such as CREATE INDEX implicitly commit before and after execution. This ensures a new transaction starts.

Option D. SELECT FOR UPDATE after CREATE TABLE AS SELECT

  • Correct because CREATE TABLE AS SELECT is a DDL operation that implicitly commits. The subsequent SELECT FOR UPDATE is a DML statement that initiates a new transaction.

Option F. First DML after COMMIT or ROLLBACK

  • Correct because Oracle transactions are implicit. After a COMMIT or ROLLBACK, the next DML statement automatically starts a new transaction.

Incorrect

Option A. CREATE TABLE after SELECT

  • Incorrect because a SELECT does not start a transaction. The CREATE TABLE is a DDL statement that implicitly commits, but this does not guarantee a new transaction in this context.

Option C. TRUNCATE after SELECT

  • Incorrect because TRUNCATE is a DDL operation that implicitly commits before and after execution. It does not start a new transaction in the same way DML does.

Option E. DML after a failed DML

  • Incorrect because a failed DML does not end the transaction. The transaction remains active until explicitly committed or rolled back, so issuing another DML continues the same transaction.

Correct

questions.preview: Which three statements are true about undo segments and the use of undo by trans
questions.question_html:
Question 37 of 60
37. Question

Which three statements are true about undo segments and the use of undo by transactions in an Oracle database instance? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

The three true statements about undo segments and their use by transactions in an Oracle database are:

Undo segments can wrap around to the first extent when a transaction fills the last extent of the undo segment. This circular allocation model allows for efficient reuse of undo space within a segment, even when it reaches its initial capacity. When a transaction fills the last extent, it can continue to use space from the beginning of the segment, overwriting older undo data that is no longer needed.

An undo segment may be used by multiple transactions simultaneously. Undo segments are shared resources, and multiple transactions can concurrently use the same segment to store their undo information. This allows for efficient utilization of undo space and avoids the overhead of creating multiple segments for each transaction.

Undo segments can extend when a transaction fills the last extent of the undo segment. If a transaction requires more undo space than is available in the current extents of a segment, Oracle can dynamically allocate additional extents to the segment to accommodate the transaction‘s needs. This ensures that transactions have sufficient undo space to complete successfully, even with large or complex operations.

Here‘s why the other statements are incorrect:

Undo segments have a minimum of three extents: This is not a strict rule. Undo segments can be created with a single extent, and the number of extents can vary depending on configuration and usage patterns.
A single transaction may use multiple undo segments simultaneously: Transactions typically use a single undo segment to maintain consistency and manage rollback operations efficiently. However, in rare cases, Oracle might allocate multiple segments for a transaction if it encounters specific conditions or resource constraints.
Undo segments must be stored in a SMALLFILE tablespace: Undo segments can reside in both SMALLFILE and BIGFILE tablespaces. The choice depends on your storage requirements, file management preferences, and overall database configuration.

Question 41 of 60
41. Question

The ORCL database has RESUMABLE_TIMEOUT = 7200 and DEFERRED_SEGMENT_CREATION = FALSE
User U1 has a 1 MB quota in tablespace DATA.
U1 executes this command:
SQL> CREATE TABLE t1 AS –
(SELECT object_name, sharing, created
FROM dba_objects);
U1 complains that the command is taking too long to execute.
In the alert log, the database administrator (DBA) finds this:
2017-03-06T12:15:17.183438+05:30
statement in resumable session ‘User U1(136), Session 1, Instance 1‘ was suspended due to ORA-01536: space quota exceeded for tablespace ‘DATA‘
Which are three actions any one of which the DBA could take to resume the session? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

The error in alert log is about the tablespace quota so either space has to be freed up or quota has to be increased.
RESUMABLE_TIMEOUT enables or disables resumable statements and specifies resumable timeout at the system level.
Resumable space allocation is only possible when statements are executed within a session that has resumable mode enabled.
Resumable space allocation is enabled for a session when the ALTER SESSION ENABLE RESUMABLE statement is executed, and the RESUMABLE_TIMEOUT initialization parameter is set to a non-zero value for the session. When the RESUMABLE_TIMEOUT initialization parameter is set at the system level, it is the default for an ALTER SESSION ENABLE RESUMABLE statement that does not specify a timeout value. When an ALTER SESSION ENABLE RESUMABLE statement specifies a timeout value, it overrides the system default.
Read here – About Enabling and Disabling Resumable Space Allocation
DEFERRED_SEGMENT_CREATION doesnt play a role here.
DEFERRED_SEGMENT_CREATION specifies the semantics of deferred segment creation.
If set to true, then segments for tables and their dependent objects (LOBs, indexes) will not be created until the first row is inserted into the table.
Before creating a set of tables, if it is known that a significant number of them will not be populated, then consider setting this parameter to true. This saves disk space and minimizes install time.

questions.question_html:
Question 43 of 60
43. Question

Which three statements are true about advanced connection options supported by Oracle Net for connection to Oracle Database instances? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

First, we need to understand the basics here.
Connect Time Failover and Transparent Application Failover (TAF) are 2 different features.
Connect-Time Failover:
It requires 2 or more listener addresses in the TNS string.
It enables a new connection to an alternate listener address during the connection attempt if the first listener address in the TNS string is not available to connect to. If you already are connected to a database, then it plays no role. Also, as it is a connect-time feature, it has nothing to do with a specific driver.
It is achieved by adding FAILOVER=ON at the top of the TNS string.
Transparent Application Failover (TAF):
It requires 1 or more listener addresses in the TNS string.
It enables the automatic re-connection of an already connected session to an alternate database/service in the TNS string if the currently connected database/service become unavailable.
TAF involves manual configuration of a network service name that includes the FAILOVER_MODE parameter (TYPE, METHOD, RETRIES, DELAY) included in the CONNECT_DATA section of the connect descriptor.
With FAILOVER_TYPE=SELECT, if there is an ongoing SELECT, then SELECT will restart with the new connection in a transparent manner to the end user. If there is ongoing DML, then the active transactions will roll back.
With FAILOVER_TYPE=SESSION, only connection is established again and nothing else is done.
With FAILOVER_TYPE=NONE, nothing is done.
Read here – What Transparent Application Failover Restores
– What Transparent Application Failover Restores
– Implementing Transparent Application Failover
–
Transparent Application Failover (TAF) is a feature of the Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) Oracle Call Interface (OCI) driver.
Read here – Enabling Advanced Features of Oracle Net Services
Load Balancing can balance the number of connections to dispatchers when using a Shared Server configuration. That‘s true.
Read here – Shared Server Configuration for an Oracle RAC Database
SOURCE_ROUTE – When set to on, this parameter instructs Oracle Net to use each address in the order presented until the destination is reached.
Read here – About the Address List Parameters

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

The generation of UNDO generates REDO  True  On a DML of Update or Delete, old image of data goes to UNDO and the change vectors for the DML are written to REDO.

questions.preview: Which two statements are true about Enterprise Manager Database Express? (Choose
questions.question_html:
Question 46 of 60
46. Question

Which two statements are true about Enterprise Manager Database Express? (Choose two.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

The two correct statements about Enterprise Manager Database Express (EM Express):

1. The same port number can be used for Database Express configurations for databases on different hosts. This is true. EM Express relies on HTTP or HTTPS protocols for communication, and ports used for these protocols can be configured independently for different Database Express instances running on different hosts. This allows you to access multiple EM Express instances without port conflicts.

2. It is available only when the database is open. This is also accurate. EM Express requires the target database to be open and accessible for it to gather information and display metrics. If the database is closed, EM Express will not be able to connect and will be unavailable.

Here‘s why the other statements are incorrect:

The same port number can be used for multiple Database Express configurations for multiple databases on the same host: This is not recommended. While technically possible in some situations, using the same port for multiple EM Express instances on the same host can lead to conflicts and interfere with their operation. It‘s generally advisable to assign different ports for each EM Express instance on the same host to avoid such issues.
It can be used to switch a database into ARCHIVELOGMODE: This is not a primary function of EM Express. While you can view database information like the current archive log mode through EM Express, it doesn‘t directly offer functionality to switch the database mode. This would require using other Oracle tools or commands like ALTER DATABASE.
It can be used to perform database recovery: Similar to switching archive log mode, EM Express primarily serves as a monitoring and management tool. It provides information about database status and metrics but doesn‘t offer features for directly performing database recovery operations. You would need other tools or commands like RECOVER DATABASE for such tasks.

questions.question_html:
Question 4 of 60
4. Question

Which three statements are true about sequences in a single instance Oracle database? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

Here are the three true statements about sequences in a single instance Oracle database:

A sequence can issue duplicate values. While sequences are primarily used to generate unique values, under certain circumstances, they can produce duplicates. This can happen due to caching mechanisms, rollbacks, or manual adjustments to the sequence‘s current value. It‘s essential to be aware of this possibility and implement appropriate measures if uniqueness is a strict requirement for your application.

A sequence‘s unallocated cached values are lost if the instance shuts down. Sequences often cache a range of values in memory for performance reasons. However, if the database instance shuts down unexpectedly, these cached values are not persisted and will be lost. New values will be generated from the last persisted value when the instance restarts, potentially leading to gaps in the sequence.

Sequences can always have gaps. Even though sequences are designed to create a continuous stream of numbers, gaps can occur due to various reasons:

Rollbacks of transactions that had already generated sequence numbers.
Manual adjustments to the sequence‘s current value.
Instances where a sequence is shared across multiple sessions and some numbers are not used.
Unexpected instance shutdowns, as mentioned earlier.
Here‘s why the other statements are incorrect:

Two or more tables cannot have keys generated from the same sequence: This is not true. Multiple tables can share the same sequence to generate their primary keys, ensuring consistency and coordination across different tables.
A sequence number that was allocated can be rolled back if a transaction fails: This is not entirely accurate. While the sequence number itself cannot be rolled back, its usage within a transaction can be reverted. However, the sequence will have already moved on to the next value, potentially creating a gap.
A sequence can only be dropped by a DBA: This is not true. Any user with the appropriate privileges can drop a sequence, not just DBAs.

questions.question_html:
Question 5 of 60
5. Question

You execute this command:
CREATE SMALLFILE TABLESPACE sales
DATAFILE ‘/u01/app/oracle/sales01.dbf‘
SIZE 5G
SEGMENT SPACE MANAGEMENT AUTO;
Which two statements are true about the SALES tablespace? (Choose two.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

The two true statements about the SALES tablespace are:

It is a locally managed tablespace: This is indicated by the SEGMENT SPACE MANAGEMENT AUTO clause in the CREATE TABLESPACE statement. Locally managed tablespaces handle their own extent management within the tablespace, rather than relying on the data dictionary for extent tracking.

It uses the database default blocksize: The absence of a specific BLOCKSIZE clause in the statement implies that the tablespace will adopt the database‘s default blocksize setting. This determines the size of data blocks used for storing data in the tablespace.

Here‘s why the other statements are incorrect:

It must be smaller than the smallest BIGFILE tablespace: This is not a requirement for smallfile tablespaces. While bigfile tablespaces can be larger in size, there‘s no restriction on smallfile tablespaces being smaller than them.
Any data files added to the tablespace must have a size of 5 gigabytes: This is also incorrect. The initial data file is created with a size of 5GB, but subsequent data files added to the tablespace can have different sizes as needed.
Free space is managed using freelists: This is not accurate for locally managed tablespaces. They use bitmaps to track free space within data blocks, providing more efficient space management compared to freelists, which are used in dictionary-managed tablespaces.

The valid query is:

Here‘s why it‘s valid:

GROUP BY clause: It correctly groups the results by both prod_id and release_date, ensuring that the SUM(cost) aggregation is performed within each unique combination of those two columns.
Non-aggregated columns: The prod_id and release_date columns are included in the SELECT clause and also in the GROUP BY clause, which is required for non-aggregated columns in a query with a GROUP BY clause.
Aggregate function: The SUM(cost) function is used appropriately to calculate the total cost for each group, providing meaningful summary information.

questions.preview: Which three statements are true about connection strings and service names used
questions.question_html:
Question 10 of 60
10. Question

Which three statements are true about connection strings and service names used to connect to an Oracle database instance? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

The three true statements about connection strings and service names in Oracle database connections are:

A single connection string can refer to multiple database instances. This is possible through the use of load balancing or failover mechanisms, where a single service name can be mapped to multiple instances to distribute load or provide redundancy.

Different connection strings in the same tnsnames.ora file can contain the same service name, host, and port parameters. This allows for different connection configurations for the same service name, potentially using different credentials, security settings, or session properties.

A single database instance can support connections for multiple service names. An instance can be associated with multiple service names, each potentially having different configuration options, access controls, or routing rules.

Here‘s why the other statements are incorrect:

A connection string must include the SID of a database instance: This is not always true. While a SID (System Identifier) can be used in a connection string, a more flexible approach is to use service names, which provide greater abstraction and can be configured to point to different instances or manage load balancing.
A service name is created by a listener: This is not accurate. Service names are defined in the database configuration, typically using the SERVICE_NAMES parameter in the instance initialization file. The listener, on the other hand, maps service names to network addresses and port numbers, enabling clients to connect.
A connection string including a service name must be defined in the tnsnames.ora file: This is not strictly required. While the tnsnames.ora file is a common way to store connection definitions, it‘s also possible to specify a service name directly in the connection string, or use other configuration methods like directory naming or external naming services.

questions.preview: Which two statements are true about a self join? (Choose two.)
questions.question_html:
Question 11 of 60
11. Question

Which two statements are true about a self join? (Choose two.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

The two true statements about a self join are:

It can be an inner join. A self join can be an inner join where rows are only kept if they have matching values in the joined columns on both sides. For example, you might find employees who report to other employees within the same organization using an inner self join on the “manager_id“ and “employee_id“ columns.
It can be a left outer join. A self join can also be a left outer join where all rows from the left table are kept, even if there‘s no match in the joined column on the right side. For example, you might want to see all employees and their managers (or “NULL“ if they have no manager) using a left outer self join on the “manager_id“ and “employee_id“ columns.
Here‘s why the other statements are incorrect:

It must be a full outer join: This is not true. A self join can be any type of join, including inner, left outer, right outer, or full outer, depending on your desired outcome.
It must be an equijoin: While self joins often use equijoins (matching values in the joined columns), it‘s not a requirement. You could potentially use other join conditions like comparisons or inequalities when appropriate.
The join key column must have an index: This is generally good practice for performance reasons, but not mandatory. Having an index on the join key can significantly improve the efficiency of a self join, especially for large datasets. However, it‘s still possible to perform a self join without an index, though it might be slower.

18. Question

Which three statements are true about using SQL*Plus? (Choose three.)

  • 1.

Correct

The three true statements about using SQL*Plus are:

It can run scripts entered at the SQL prompt. SQL*Plus provides an interactive environment where you can type SQL commands and scripts directly at the prompt, execute them, and view the results.

It can run scripts passed to it by a shell script. SQL*Plus can also be executed from the command line, allowing you to pass scripts as arguments. This enables automation and integration with other tools and scripts.

It has its own commands that are separate from any SQL statements. SQLPlus has a set of built-in commands that control its behavior, formatting, and output. These commands are distinct from SQL statements and are used to manage the SQLPlus environment itself.

Here‘s why the other statements are incorrect:

It must be downloaded from the Oracle Technology Network (OTN). This is not true. SQL*Plus is typically included as part of the standard Oracle Database installation. You don‘t need to download it separately from OTN.
It can run Recovery Manager (RMAN) commands. This is incorrect. RMAN is a separate utility with its own command-line interface. SQL*Plus is primarily used for executing SQL statements and interacting with database objects.
It has both command-line and graphical user interfaces (GUI). SQLPlus is a command-line tool. It does not have a built-in graphical user interface. However, there are third-party GUI tools that can interact with SQLPlus.

Question 19 of 60
19. Question

You want to apply the principle of Least Privilege in all your live databases.
One of your requirements is to revoke unnecessary privileges from all users who have them using Privilege Analysis.
Which three are types of analyses can be done using the DBMS_PRIVILEGE_CAPTURE package? (Choose two.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

Correct:

Option A. analysis of privileges granted directly to a role that are then used by a user who has been granted that role
DBMS_PRIVILEGE_CAPTURE supports capturing privileges used through roles, including system and object privileges that are granted directly to a role and subsequently exercised by users who hold that role. This is a core use case for privilege analysis when applying the least-privilege principle.

Option E. analysis of privileges granted indirectly to a role that are then used by a user who has been granted that role
Privilege Analysis can also capture indirect role privileges (role-to-role grants). If a role inherits privileges from another role and a user exercises those privileges, DBMS_PRIVILEGE_CAPTURE can record this usage, making this option valid.

Incorrect:

Option B. analysis of privileges that a user has on other schema’s objects
DBMS_PRIVILEGE_CAPTURE does not perform analysis based on object ownership boundaries (other schemas vs. own schema). It captures privileges actually used, not categorization by schema ownership.

Option C. analysis of privileges that a user has on their own schema objects
Privileges on a user’s own objects are implicitly available and are not subject to privilege analysis capture for revocation purposes, so this is not a supported analysis type.

Option D. analysis of all privileges used by the SYS user
Privilege analysis explicitly excludes the SYS user. SYS operates with unrestricted privileges, and its activity is not captured by DBMS_PRIVILEGE_CAPTURE.

Correct

  • Option B: Enabling Unified Auditing Explanation: Consolidates audit records into a single repository, improves performance, and is Oracle’s recommended auditing framework.
  • Option C: Revoking execute privilege on UTL_ packages from PUBLIC* Explanation: Prevents misuse of powerful network packages by untrusted users. Oracle recommends revoking these from PUBLIC.
  • Option F: Using Access Control Lists (ACLs) Explanation: Provides fine-grained control over which users or applications can access external network services.

Correct

Option C. Local Naming requires setting the TNS_ADMIN environment variable on the client side

  • Correct. Local naming uses tnsnames.ora files, and the TNS_ADMIN variable is often set to specify the directory containing these files.

Option D. A client can connect to an Oracle database instance even if no client side network admin has been configured

  • Correct. This is possible using the Easy Connect naming method, which allows connections without requiring configuration files like tnsnames.ora.

  • Incorrect. Local naming itself does not inherently provide failover; failover requires additional configuration in the connect descriptor.

  • Incorrect. Easy Connect supports TCP/IP connections, but SSL is not natively supported through Easy Connect syntax. SSL requires additional Oracle Net configuration.

26. Question

You execute this query:
SELECT TO_CHAR(NEXT_DAY(LAST_DAY(SYSDATE), ‘MON‘), ‘dd ′Monday for′ fmMonth rrrr‘)
What is the result?

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
Correct

Correct

Option D. It returns the date for the first Monday of the next month Correct because:

  • LAST_DAY(SYSDATE) returns the last day of the current month.
  • NEXT_DAY(date, 'MON') returns the next Monday after that date. Since the last day of the month is not guaranteed to be a Monday, the function will return the first Monday of the following month.
  • TO_CHAR then formats the result into the string pattern: dd Monday for Month yyyy.

Incorrect

Option A. Executes successfully but no result Incorrect because the query does return a valid date string. It does not produce an empty result set.

Option B. Returns the last Monday of the current month Incorrect because NEXT_DAY does not look backward. It always finds the next occurrence of the specified day after the given date, not the last one within the same month.

Option C. Generates an error Incorrect because the query syntax is valid. Oracle supports NEXT_DAY, LAST_DAY, and TO_CHAR with the given format string. No error is generated.

Correct

  • Specifically designed for high‑volume insert operations, making it the correct choice.

Correct

Correct

FROM products

questions.preview: Which three statements are true about Deferred Segment Creation in Oracle databa
questions.question_html:
Question 30 of 60
30. Question

Which three statements are true about Deferred Segment Creation in Oracle databases? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

Correct

Option B: Sessions may dynamically switch back and forth from DEFERRED to IMMEDIATE segment creation

  • Correct because: Oracle allows sessions to toggle between DEFERRED (segments created only when data is inserted) and IMMEDIATE (segments created at object creation).
  • This flexibility lets DBAs control storage allocation depending on workload or testing needs.

Option C: It is the default behavior for tables and indexes

  • Correct because: Since Oracle Database 11g, Deferred Segment Creation is the default for non-partitioned heap tables and indexes in locally managed tablespaces.
  • This reduces unnecessary storage allocation for empty objects.

Option D: Indexes inherit the DEFERRED to IMMEDIATE segment creation attribute from their parent table

  • Correct because: When a table is created with deferred segment creation, its associated indexes also inherit the same attribute.
  • This ensures consistency in storage allocation behavior across related objects.

 Incorrect

Option A: It is supported for Index Organized Tables (IOTs) contained in locally managed tablespaces

  • Incorrect because Deferred Segment Creation is not supported for IOTs.
  • IOTs require immediate segment creation due to their storage structure.

Option E: It is supported for SYS-owned tables contained in locally managed tablespaces

  • Incorrect because SYS-owned objects are excluded from deferred segment creation.
  • System tables must always allocate segments immediately to ensure database stability.

questions.preview: Which two statements are true about Enterprise Manager (EM) Express?
questions.question_html:
Question 34 of 60
34. Question

Which two statements are true about Enterprise Manager (EM) Express?

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

The two correct statements about Enterprise Manager (EM) Express are:

By default, EM Express is available for a database after database creation using DBCA: When you create a database using Database Configuration Assistant (DBCA), EM Express is automatically configured and enabled, making it readily accessible for monitoring and managing the new database instance.
You cannot start up a database instance using EM Express: EM Express primarily serves as a monitoring and management tool. While it provides information about database status and operations, it doesn‘t offer functionality for directly controlling database startup or shutdown. You would need to use other tools or commands like STARTUP/SHUTDOWN IMMEDIATE for such actions.
Here‘s why the other statements are incorrect:

EM Express uses a separate repository database to store target database metadata: EM Express typically utilizes the internal metadata repository within the target database itself to gather information and display metrics. It doesn‘t require a separate repository database in most cases.
You can shut down a database instance using EM Express: As mentioned earlier, EM Express focuses on monitoring and management, not direct control over database operations. You cannot use it to initiate shutdowns, although you can view the current status and receive alerts related to shutdowns initiated through other means.
You can use a single instance of EM Express to manage multiple database running on the same server: This is generally true. A single EM Express instance can monitor and manage multiple databases hosted on the same server, providing a consolidated view of their performance and health.

Correct

The WITH CHECK clause has no effect when deleting rows from the underlying table through the view.  True (mostly)
Quoting Oracle Docs:
For a DELETE statement, if the join results in more than one key-preserved table, then Oracle Database deletes from the first table named in the FROM clause, whether or not the view was created WITH CHECK OPTION.
Views cannot be used to add or modify rows in an underlying table if the defining query of the view contains the DISTINCT keyword.  True
Quoting Oracle Docs:
For a view to be inherently updatable, the following conditions must be met:
The view must not contain any of the following constructs:
A DISTINCT operator
Views cannot be used to add rows to an underlying table if the table has columns with NOT NULL constraints lacking default values which are not referenced in the defining query of the view.  True
Quoting Oracle Docs:
For you to insert into the table using the view, the view must contain all NOT NULL columns of all tables in the join, unless you have specified DEFAULT values for the NOT NULL columns.

Which two queries execute successfully? (Choose two.)

The two queries that will execute successfully are:

SELECT NVL2(cust_credit_limit, TO_CHAR(cust_credit_limit * .15), ‘Not Available‘) FROM customers;
SELECT NVL(TO_CHAR(cust_credit_limit * .15), ‘Not Available‘) FROM customers;
Here‘s why these queries work and the others don‘t:

NVL2(cust_credit_limit * .15, ‘Not Available‘) FROM customers: This query won‘t execute because NVL2 expects three arguments: expression1, expression2, and expression3. In this case, only two arguments are provided, leading to a syntax error.
SELECT TO_CHAR(NVL(cust_credit_limit * .15, ‘Not Available‘)) FROM customers: This query attempts to convert a string (‘Not Available‘) to a character using TO_CHAR, which is unnecessary as it‘s already a string. It also creates potential issues if cust_credit_limit is NULL, as NVL would return ‘Not Available‘, and TO_CHAR might not handle it as expected.
SELECT NVL(cust_credit_limit * .15, ‘Not Available‘) FROM customers: This query correctly uses NVL to handle potential NULL values in cust_credit_limit. If the value is NULL, it displays ‘Not Available‘; otherwise, it performs the multiplication and displays the result.

Correct

Upon execution, the command will succeed, and the following will happen:

Connection to the Database Instance: The command sqlplus initiates a connection to the database. It uses the credentials hr/hr to authenticate the user HR and specifies @orcl to connect to the database instance named orcl.

Script Execution: The @abc.sql portion instructs SQLPlus to execute the SQL script named abc.sql immediately after establishing the connection. It‘s assumed that abc.sql resides in the current working directory or a path accessible to SQLPlus.

Here‘s a breakdown of the key elements in the command:

sqlplus: This is the command-line tool used to interact with Oracle databases.
hr/hr: This provides the username (HR) and password (also HR) for authentication.
@orcl: This designates the database instance to connect to.
@abc.sql: This signals SQL*Plus to execute the specified script file.
Key points to remember:

Single @ for Script Execution: The @ symbol is used only once for script execution, not for database connection.
Full Path Optional: If the script is in the current working directory, the full path isn‘t necessary. However, specifying the full path ensures clarity and avoids potential errors if the script is located elsewhere.

questions.question_html:
Question 43 of 60
43. Question

Table ORDER_ITEMS contains columns ORDER_ID, UNIT_PRICE and QUANTITY, of data type NUMBER.
Examine these SQL statements:
Statement 1:
SELECT MAX(unit_price * quantity) “Maximum Order“
FROM order_items;
Statement 2:
SELECT MAX(unit_price * quantity) “Maximum Order“
FROM order_items –
GROUP BY order_id;
Which two statements are true?

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

The two true statements about the SQL statements are:

Statement 1 returns only one row of output. This is because it uses the MAX function to find the maximum value of unit_price * quantity across all rows in the table, without any grouping. It returns a single aggregate value representing the overall maximum order value.

Statement 2 may return multiple rows of output. This is because it uses the GROUP BY clause to group the data by ORDER_ID before applying the MAX function. It calculates the maximum order value within each order_id group, potentially resulting in multiple rows of output, one for each distinct order_id.

Here‘s why the other statements are incorrect:

Statement 2 returns only one row of output: This is not always true. It depends on the number of distinct ORDER_ID values in the table. If there are multiple order_ids, it will produce multiple rows.
Both the statements give the same output: This is only true if there‘s a single order_id in the table. Otherwise, they produce different results due to the grouping in Statement 2.
Both statements will return NULL if either UNIT_PRICE or QUANTITY contains NULL: This is not accurate. MAX generally ignores NULL values during calculation. If all values in a group are NULL, then MAX will return NULL, but not if only some of them are NULL.

Correct

The shrink clause lets you manually shrink space in a table, index-organized table or its overflow segment, index, partition, subpartition, LOB segment, materialized view, or materialized view log. This clause is valid only for segments in tablespaces with automatic segment management. By default, Oracle Database compacts the segment, adjusts the high water mark, and releases the recuperated space immediately.
Compacting the segment requires row movement. Therefore, you must enable row movement for the object you want to shrink before specifying this clause. Further, if your application has any rowid-based triggers, you should disable them before issuing this clause.

NULLIF compares expr1 and expr2. If they are equal, then the function returns null. If they are not equal, then the function returns expr1. You cannot specify the literal NULL for expr1.

If the arguments are not numeric, then they must be of the same data type, or Oracle returns an error.

The three correct statements about Oracle synonyms:

A SEQUENCE can have a synonym. This is true. You can create synonyms for sequences just like you can for other database objects. This can be helpful for simplifying long or complex sequence names and improving code readability.
A synonym created by one user can refer to an object belonging to another user. This is also true. When you create a synonym, you can specify the schema of the object you‘re referencing. This allows you to create synonyms for objects owned by other users, making it easier to access those objects in your own code.
A synonym can be available to all users. This is true for public synonyms. When you create a public synonym, it becomes accessible to all users of the database. This can be useful for making commonly used objects easy to find and use.

Any user can drop a PUBLIC synonym: This is not true. Only users with the DROP SYNONYM privilege or the owner of the synonym can drop a public synonym.

This allows you to create synonyms for objects owned by other users, making it easier to access those objects in your own code.
A synonym can be available to all users. This is true for public synonyms. When you create a public synonym, it becomes accessible to all users of the database. This can be useful for making commonly used objects easy to find and use.

Segment creation is not deferred.

Correct

Here are the three statements that must be true for the SALES user to create tables in SALES_Q1:

The sales user must have a quota on the SALES_Q1 tablespace to hold the initial extends of all tables they plan to create in their schema. A quota is a limit on the amount of space a user can consume within a tablespace. To create tables, a user must have a sufficient quota in the designated tablespace to accommodate the initial extents (basic storage allocations) of those tables.

The sales user must have been granted the CREATE TABLE privilege. This privilege is essential for users to create new tables in the database. It‘s a specific privilege that needs to be granted explicitly, as it‘s not included in general database access privileges.

The sales user must have been granted the CREATE SESSION privilege. This privilege is required for users to establish a connection to the database and perform any operations within it. Without CREATE SESSION, users cannot interact with the database, even if they have other privileges.

Here‘s why the other statements are not necessary:

The sales user must have a quota on the TEMP tablespace: A quota on the temporary tablespace is not a prerequisite for creating tables. The temporary tablespace is used for temporary data storage during database operations, not for permanent table storage.
The sales user must have their quota on the users tablespace removed: The user‘s quota on the USERS tablespace, if any, doesn‘t directly affect their ability to create tables in SALES_Q1. Quotas are tablespace-specific, so removing a quota from one tablespace doesn‘t grant privileges in another.
The sales user must have a quota on the SALES_Q1 tablespace to hold all the rows to be inserted into any table in their schema: While ensuring sufficient space for future data growth is important, it‘s not strictly required for table creation. A descending index is a type of function-based index.  True

questions.question_html:
Question 60 of 60
60. Question

Examine the description of the SALES1 table:

SALES2 is a table with the same description as SALES1.

Some sales data is contained erroneously in both tables.

You must display rows from SALES1 and SALES2 and wish to see the duplicates too.

Which set operator generates the required output?

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

The best set operator for your scenario is:

UNION ALL

Here‘s why:

UNION: This would only display distinct rows, removing duplicates from both tables. While it might provide unique data, it wouldn‘t fulfill your requirement of seeing all rows, including duplicates.
MINUS: This would show rows in SALES1 that are not present in SALES2, not the duplicates you need.
INTERSECT: This would only show rows present in both SALES1 and SALES2, excluding the erroneous data in each table individually.
SUBTRACT: This operator isn‘t applicable in this context as it involves subtracting columns, not entire rows.
UNION ALL combines all rows from both SALES1 and SALES2 without eliminating duplicates. This allows you to see all data, including the erroneously duplicated rows present in both tables.

questions.question_html:
Question 10 of 60
10. Question

In the ORCL database, UNDOTBS1 is the active undo tablespace with these properties:
1. A size of 100 MB
2. AUTOEXTEND is off
3. UNDO_RETENTION is set to 15 minutes
4. It has RETENTION GUARANTEE
UNDOTBS1 fills with uncommitted undo 10 minutes after the database opens.
What will happen when the next update is attempted by any transaction?

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

Explanation
As UNDO is already filled up and AUTOEXTEND is off, the next transaction will cause error. The parameter UNDO_RETENTION is not playing any role in this scenario.
Starting with Oracle Database release 19c, version 19.7, for both AUTOEXTEND undo tablespaces and fixed-size undo tablespaces, the system retains undo for at least the time specified in this parameter, and automatically tunes the undo retention period to satisfy the undo requirements of the queries.
In earlier versions of Oracle Database release 19c, the behavior is different for the two types of undo tablespaces. For AUTOEXTEND undo tablespaces, the system retains undo for at least the time specified in this parameter, and automatically tunes the undo retention period to satisfy the undo requirements of the queries. For fixed-size undo tablespaces, the system automatically tunes for the maximum possible undo retention period, based on undo tablespace size and usage history, and ignores UNDO_RETENTION unless retention guarantee is enabled for the tablespace

This value reserves 10% of each block for updates to existing rows and allows inserts of new rows to fill a maximum of 90% of each block.

A block becomes a candidate for row insertion when its used space falls below PCTUSED.

questions.preview: Which three statements are true about table data storage in an Oracle Database?
questions.question_html:
Question 18 of 60
18. Question

Which three statements are true about table data storage in an Oracle Database? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

Correct:

Option B. Multiple row pieces from the same row may be stored in different database blocks
Oracle supports row chaining and row migration. If a row is too large to fit into a single data block, or if it grows after an update, Oracle can split the row into multiple row pieces and store them in different database blocks. Pointers are maintained so Oracle can reconstruct the row during retrieval.

Option D. Data block headers contain their own Data Block Address (DBA)
Each Oracle data block includes a block header that stores metadata about the block. This metadata includes the Data Block Address (DBA), which uniquely identifies the block within the database and is required for internal block management and consistency checks.

Option F. A table row piece can be chained across several database blocks
When a row is larger than the available space in a single block, Oracle chains the row across multiple blocks. Each block contains a row piece, and Oracle follows pointers between blocks to access the complete row. This is a normal and supported behavior in Oracle storage architecture.

Incorrect:

Option A. Multiple row pieces from the same row may be stored in the same block
Within a single data block, a row is stored as one contiguous row piece. Oracle does not split a row into multiple row pieces within the same block. Row pieces only occur across blocks, not within a single block.

Option C. Data block free space is always contiguous in the middle of the block
Free space in a data block is not always contiguous and is not guaranteed to be in the middle. As rows are inserted, updated, or deleted, free space can become fragmented within the block. Oracle manages this space dynamically using block internals such as the row directory.

Option E. Index block free space is always contiguous in the middle of the block
Index blocks, like table data blocks, can have fragmented free space due to inserts and deletes. Free space in index blocks is not guaranteed to be contiguous or centrally located, making this statement incorrect.

questions.question_html:
Question 23 of 60
23. Question

Which four account management capabilities can be configured using Oracle profiles? (Choose four.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

Correct

Option A. The number of hours for which an account is locked after the configured number of login attempts has been reached

  • Profiles allow configuration of FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS and PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME, which define how long an account remains locked after failed login attempts.

Option B. The ability to prevent a password from ever being reused

  • Profiles can enforce PASSWORD_REUSE_MAX and PASSWORD_REUSE_TIME. Setting these appropriately can prevent password reuse entirely.

Option D. The number of days for which an account may be inactive before it is locked

  • Profiles support INACTIVE_ACCOUNT_TIME, which locks accounts after a defined period of inactivity.

Option F. The number of days for which an account is locked after the configured number of login attempts has been reached

  • This is another way of expressing PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME, which specifies the duration of account lock after failed login attempts.

Incorrect

Option C. The number of password changes required within a period of time before a password can be reused

  • Profiles do not enforce a specific number of password changes within a time period before reuse. Instead, reuse is controlled by PASSWORD_REUSE_MAX and PASSWORD_REUSE_TIME.

Option E. The maximum amount of CPU time allowed for a user’s sessions before their account is locked

  • Profiles can limit CPU_PER_SESSION or CPU_PER_CALL, but exceeding these does not lock the account. It only terminates the session or call.

Incorrect

Correct

questions.preview: Which two statements are true about space-saving features in an Oracle Database?
questions.question_html:
Question 25 of 60
25. Question

Which two statements are true about space-saving features in an Oracle Database? (Choose two.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

Correct

Option A. Private Temporary Tables (PTTs) store metadata in memory only

  • Correct because Private Temporary Tables (PTTs) are session‑specific and their metadata is stored in memory, not in the data dictionary.
  • This reduces space usage and improves performance since metadata does not persist beyond the session.

Option E. An index created with the UNUSABLE attribute has no segment

  • Correct because when an index is created with the UNUSABLE attribute, Oracle does not allocate a segment for it.
  • This saves space until the index is rebuilt or made usable.

Incorrect

Option B. If they exist for a session, Private Temporary Tables (PTTs) are always dropped at the next COMMIT OR ROLLBACK statement

  • Incorrect because PTTs persist for the duration of the session unless explicitly dropped.
  • They are not automatically dropped at COMMIT or ROLLBACK.

Option C. A table that is truncated will always have its segment removed

  • Incorrect because truncating a table removes rows but retains the segment for reuse.
  • The segment is not dropped; only the data is cleared.

Option D. An index that is altered to be UNUSABLE will retain its segment

  • Incorrect because altering an index to UNUSABLE does not drop the segment, but the statement here is misleading.
  • The space is not reclaimed, but the index cannot be used until rebuilt.

questions.preview: You need to calculate the number of days from 1 January 2019 until today. Dates
questions.question_html:
Question 26 of 60
26. Question

You need to calculate the number of days from 1 January 2019 until today. Dates are stored in the default format of DD-MON-RR. Which two queries give the required output? (Choose two.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

Correct

Option B. SELECT SYSDATE - TO_DATE('01-JANUARY-2019') FROM DUAL;

  • Correct because TO_DATE converts the string '01-JANUARY-2019' into a valid Oracle DATE datatype.
  • Subtracting this from SYSDATE returns the number of days between the two dates.
  • This query works without rounding, giving the exact difference in days.

Option E. SELECT ROUND(SYSDATE - TO_DATE('01/JANUARY/2019')) FROM DUAL;

  • Correct because this query also uses TO_DATE to convert the string into a DATE value.
  • Subtracting gives the difference in days, and ROUND ensures the result is rounded to the nearest whole number.
  • This is valid and produces the required output.

Incorrect

Option A. SELECT TO_DATE(SYSDATE, 'DD/MONTH/YYYY') - '01/JANUARY/2019' FROM DUAL;

  • Incorrect because SYSDATE is already a DATE, and using TO_DATE on it is invalid.
  • Also, '01/JANUARY/2019' is treated as a string literal, not converted properly into a DATE.

Option C. SELECT ROUND(SYSDATE - '01-JAN-2019') FROM DUAL;

  • Incorrect because '01-JAN-2019' is a string literal, not a DATE.
  • Oracle requires explicit conversion using TO_DATE. Without it, this query fails.

Option D. SELECT TO_CHAR(SYSDATE, 'DD-MON-YYYY') - '01-JAN-2019' FROM DUAL;

  • Incorrect because TO_CHAR converts SYSDATE into a string, not a DATE.
  • Subtracting strings is invalid in Oracle SQL.

27. Question

Which three statements are true about data block storage in an Oracle Database? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

Correct

Option B. An index block can contain row data.

  • Correct because index blocks store key values and pointers to row data.
  • While they don’t store full table rows, they do contain references (rowids) that point to the actual row data in table blocks.

Option C. Row data is stored starting at the end of the block.

  • Correct because Oracle stores row data from the end of the block moving backward, while the block header and row directory grow from the beginning of the block forward.
  • This design allows efficient space management and row directory indexing.

Option E. A block header contains a row directory pointing to all rows in the block.

  • Correct because the block header includes metadata such as the row directory, transaction slots, and free space information.
  • The row directory provides pointers to the actual row data stored in the block.

Incorrect

  • Incorrect because a table block may be empty (for example, newly allocated blocks or blocks with deleted rows).
  • It is not mandatory for every table block to contain row data at all times.

  • Incorrect because the block header length can vary depending on factors such as the number of rows, transaction slots, and row directory entries.
  • It is not fixed across all blocks.

questions.question_html:
Question 29 of 60
29. Question

The ORCL database has RESUMABLE_TIMEOUT = 7200 and DEFERRED_SEGMENT_CREATION = FALSE. User U1 has a 1 MB quota in tablespace DATA. U1 executes this command:

sql
CREATE TABLE t1 AS
(SELECT object_name, sharing, created
 FROM dba_objects);

U1 complains that the command is taking too long to execute. In the alert log, the DBA finds:

Code
statement in resumable session 'User U1(136), Session 1, Instance 1'
was suspended due to ORA-01536: space quota exceeded for tablespace 'DATA'

Which are three actions any one of which the DBA could take to resume the session? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

Correct

Option A. Grant UNLIMITED TABLESPACE to U1

  • Correct because granting UNLIMITED TABLESPACE removes quota restrictions for the user.
  • This immediately resolves the quota exceeded error and allows the resumable session to continue.

Option B. Drop other U1 objects in DATA

  • Correct because dropping existing objects owned by U1 in the DATA tablespace frees up quota space.
  • Once quota is freed, the resumable session can resume execution.

Option D. Increase U1’s quota sufficiently in DATA

  • Correct because explicitly increasing U1’s quota in the DATA tablespace provides the required space.
  • This is a direct fix for the quota exceeded error.

Incorrect

Option C. Set AUTOEXTEND ON for data files in DATA

  • Incorrect because the issue is quota exceeded, not lack of physical space in the tablespace.
  • AUTOEXTEND affects tablespace size, but quotas are user‑specific limits.

Option E. Set DEFERRED_SEGMENT_CREATION to TRUE

  • Incorrect because this parameter controls whether segments are created immediately or deferred until data is inserted.
  • It does not resolve quota issues for existing operations.

Option F. Add a data file to DATA

  • Incorrect because adding a data file increases tablespace size, but the error is due to user quota exceeded, not tablespace capacity.

questions.question_html:
Question 32 of 60
32. Question

The STORES table has a column START_DATE of data type DATE, containing the date the row was inserted.
You only want to display details of rows where START_DATE is within the last 25 months.
Which WHERE clause can be used?

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
Correct

The correct WHERE clause to filter for rows with START_DATE within the last 25 months is:

WHERE MONTHS_BETWEEN(SYSDATE, start_date) <= 25 Here‘s why this clause works: MONTHS_BETWEEN function: This function calculates the number of months between two dates. It accurately handles differences in years and varying month lengths, making it ideal for date comparisons based on months.
SYSDATE: This function returns the current date and time from the database server, providing a dynamic reference point for the comparison.
start_date: This column holds the date values you want to compare against the current date.
<= 25 comparison: This ensures that only rows with START_DATE values within the last 25 months are included in the results.
Here‘s why the other options are incorrect:

WHERE TO_NUMBER(start_date – SYSDATE) <= 25: This clause subtracts SYSDATE from START_DATE, resulting in a negative number for rows within the last 25 months. Converting this to a number and comparing it to 25 wouldn‘t produce the desired results.
WHERE ADD_MONTHS(start_date, 25) <= SYSDATE: This clause adds 25 months to START_DATE, which doesn‘t filter for rows within the last 25 months but rather for rows with START_DATEs more than 25 months in the past.
WHERE MONTHS_BETWEEN(start_date, SYSDATE) <= 25: This clause has the arguments in the wrong order. It would calculate the number of months between START_DATE and SYSDATE, which is the opposite of what‘s needed for this filter.

questions.question_html:
Question 43 of 60
43. Question

Which four statements are true regarding primary and foreign key constraints and the effect they can have on table data? (Choose four.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

Explanation
CONSTRAINT clause
A CONSTRAINT clause is an optional part of a CREATE TABLE statement or ALTER TABLE statement. A constraint is a rule to which data must conform. Constraint names are optional.
A CONSTRAINT can be one of the following:
a column-level constraint
Column-level constraints refer to a single column in the table and do not specify a column name (except check constraints). They refer to the column that they follow.
a table-level constraint
Table-level constraints refer to one or more columns in the table. Table-level constraints specify the names of the columns to which they apply. Table-level CHECK constraints can refer to 0 or more columns in the table.
Column constraints include:
NOT NULL
Specifies that this column cannot hold NULL values (constraints of this type are not nameable).
PRIMARY KEY
Specifies the column that uniquely identifies a row in the table. The identified columns must be defined as NOT NULL.
Note: If you attempt to add a primary key using ALTER TABLE and any of the columns included in the primary key contain null values, an error will be generated and the primary key will not be added. See ALTER TABLE statement for more information.
UNIQUE
Specifies that values in the column must be unique.
FOREIGN KEY
Specifies that the values in the column must correspond to values in a referenced primary key or unique key column or that they are NULL.
CHECK
Specifies rules for values in the column.
Table constraints include:
PRIMARY KEY
Specifies the column or columns that uniquely identify a row in the table. NULL values are not allowed.
UNIQUE
Specifies that values in the columns must be unique.
FOREIGN KEY
Specifies that the values in the columns must correspond to values in referenced primary key or unique columns or that they are NULL.
Note: If the foreign key consists of multiple columns, and any column is NULL, the whole key is considered NULL. The insert is permitted no matter what is on the non-null columns.
CHECK
Specifies a wide range of rules for values in the table.
Column constraints and table constraints have the same function; the difference is in where you specify them. Table constraints allow you to specify more than one column in a PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, or FOREIGN KEY constraint definition. Column-level constraints (except for check constraints) refer to only one column.
Read here  Types of Integrity Constraints

No action on deletion or update

questions.preview: Which three statements are true about time zones, date data types, and timestamp
questions.question_html:
Question 49 of 60
49. Question

Which three statements are true about time zones, date data types, and timestamp data types in an Oracle database? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

Explanation
The CURRENT_TIMESTAMP function returns data without time zone information  False
CURRENT_TIMESTAMP returns the current date and time in the session time zone, in a value of data type TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE. The time zone offset reflects the current local time of the SQL session. If you omit precision, then the default is 6. The difference between this function and LOCALTIMESTAMP is that CURRENT_TIMESTAMP returns a TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE value while LOCALTIMESTAMP returns a TIMESTAMP value.
Read here – CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
A TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIMEZONE data type column is stored in the database using the time zone of the session that inserted the row  False
TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE is another variant of TIMESTAMP. It differs from TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE as follows: data stored in the database is normalized to the database time zone, and the time zone offset is not stored as part of the column data.
Read here  TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE Data Type
A TIMESTAMP data type column contains information about year, month, and day  True
Year, month, and day values of date, as well as hour, minute, and second values of time, where fractional_seconds_precision is the number of digits in the fractional part of the SECOND datetime field.
Read here  Oracle Built-in Data Types
The DBTIMEZONE function can return an offset from Universal Coordinated Time (UTC)  True
DBTIMEZONE returns the value of the database time zone. The return type is a time zone offset (a character type in the format ‘[+|-]TZH:TZM‘) or a time zone region name, depending on how the user specified the database time zone value in the most recent CREATE DATABASE or ALTER DATABASE statement.
Read here  DBTIMEZONE
The SESSIONTIMEZONE function can return an offset from Universal Coordinated Time (UTC)  True
SESSIONTIMEZONE returns the time zone of the current session. The return type is a time zone offset (a character type in the format ‘[+|-]TZH:TZM‘) or a time zone region name, depending on how the user specified the session time zone value in the most recent ALTER SESSION statement.

Question 52 of 60
52. Question

Which two statements are true regarding the UNION and UNION ALL operators? (Choose two.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
Correct

Explanation
Here‘s a breakdown of the statements regarding UNION and UNION ALL operators:

A. NULLS are not ignored during duplicate checking: This is true. Both UNION and UNION ALL consider NULL values during duplicate checking. Two rows with NULL in corresponding columns will be considered duplicates even if other values differ.
B. The names of columns selected in each SELECT statement must be identical: This is not strictly true. The column aliases (AS clause) can be different, but the number of columns and their data types must match.
C. The number of columns selected in each SELECT statement must be identical: This is true. UNION and UNION ALL require the result sets to have the same number of columns in the same order.
D. Duplicates are eliminated automatically by the UNION ALL operator: This is the key difference between UNION and UNION ALL. UNION ALL includes all rows from both queries, including duplicates.
E. The output is sorted by the UNION ALL operator: No, UNION ALL does not inherently sort the output. The order depends on how the data is retrieved from the individual queries.
Therefore, the two true statements are:

A. NULLS are not ignored during duplicate checking
C. The number of columns selected in each SELECT statement must be identical

questions.preview: Which three statements are true about advanced connection options supported by O
questions.question_html:
Question 54 of 60
54. Question

Which three statements are true about advanced connection options supported by Oracle Net for connection to Oracle Database instances? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.
  • 4.
  • 5.
  • 6.
Correct

Explanation
First, we need to understand the basics here.
Connect Time Failover and Transparent Application Failover (TAF) are 2 different features.
Connect-Time Failover:
It requires 2 or more listener addresses in the TNS string.
It enables a new connection to an alternate listener address during the connection attempt if the first listener address in the TNS string is not available to connect to. If you already are connected to a database, then it plays no role. Also, as it is a connect-time feature, it has nothing to do with a specific driver.
It is achieved by adding FAILOVER=ON at the top of the TNS string.
Transparent Application Failover (TAF):
It requires 1 or more listener addresses in the TNS string.
It enables the automatic re-connection of an already connected session to an alternate database/service in the TNS string if the currently connected database/service become unavailable.
TAF involves manual configuration of a network service name that includes the FAILOVER_MODE parameter (TYPE, METHOD, RETRIES, DELAY) included in the CONNECT_DATA section of the connect descriptor.
With FAILOVER_TYPE=SELECT, if there is an ongoing SELECT, then SELECT will restart with the new connection in a transparent manner to the end user. If there is ongoing DML, then the active transactions will roll back.
With FAILOVER_TYPE=SESSION, only connection is established again and nothing else is done.
With FAILOVER_TYPE=NONE, nothing is done.
Read here – What Transparent Application Failover Restores

Which three statements are true about the Oracle Data Dictionary? (Choose three.)

  • 1.
  • 2.
  • 3.

  • 5.

Correct

Explanation
Data Dictionary views are created by joins of dictionary base tables, not DBA-defined tables.
These are owned by SYS, not SYSTEM users.
Contents of the Data Dictionary
The data dictionary consists of base tables and views.
These objects are defined as follows:
Base tables
These store information about the database. Only Oracle Database should write to and read these tables. Users rarely access the base tables directly because they are normalized and most data is stored in a cryptic format.
Views
These decode the base table data into useful information, such as user or table names, using joins and WHERE clauses to simplify the information. The views contain the names and descriptions of all objects in the data dictionary. Some views are accessible to all database users, whereas others are intended for administrators only.

The Oracle Database user account SYS owns all base tables and user-accessible views of the data dictionary.
